en.text: Andrab Lake is a small alpine lake north of Kalam. Access is by hike in summer.

Falak Sar is a peak. It is the highest peak in Swat Valley, a 5,918 metres Hindu Kush summit seen from Ushu and Matiltan. It was first climbed in 1957 by W.K.A. Berry and C. Tyndale-Biscoe. Access is by mountaineering, with base camp via Matiltan and the Falak Sar valley.

Gabral is a Gujar-Gawri village at 2,286 metres on the Gabral River. The Gabral River meets the Utror River there. It is the gateway to Shahi Bagh, Kharkhari and Mushroom Lake. Access is by jeep road from Utror, about 7 kilometres away, or Kalam, about 20 kilometres away.

Izmis Lake is a lake above the tree line southwest of Utror, ringed by caves. It is named after the surrounding caves. A jeep link road leads part of the way from Utror. Access is by jeep to Loypanghalay, then a trek of 3 to 6 hours.
Jabba Zomalu Lake is a lake. It is remote, in the Falak Sar valley below the peak. Access is by trek.

Jamia Masjid Thal is a large timber mosque on the Panjkora bank at Thal. It is built of pure wood with huge pillars. Originally built in 1865. In 1950 a fire damaged it, and locals rebuilt it in wood. Second-floor work began in 1998 and finished about nine years later. The mosque is in Thal village and is open to respectful visitors outside prayer times.

Jandrai, also Jandarai, is a village. It is the last settlement or hut cluster on the jeep road from Kumrat before the walk up to Jahaz Banda, where the road ends. Access is by jeep from Thal or Kumrat via Darwaza and Lamoti, then trek to Jahaz Banda.

Kalam is a town and the main tourist base of upper Swat. It sits on a terrace where the Swat River forms from the Gabral, also called Utror, and Ushu rivers. It is the road head for Ushu, Matiltan, Mahodand, Utror and Gabral. Kalam lies 99 kilometres north of Mingora at about 2,000 metres. It is mainly inhabited by Gawri people. The N-95 from Mingora takes about 3 to 4 hours. The road is open most of the year, with snow in winter.
Katora Lake is a bowl-shaped alpine glacial lake above Jahaz Banda. Its name comes from its shape. It is reached by trek from Jahaz Banda in summer.

Kharkhari Lake is a small lake-like widening of the Gabral stream in the upper Gabral valley. It is about 400 metres long and 250 metres wide. A jeep road reaches it, roughly 41 kilometres from Kalam, in summer.

Kundol Lake is a glacier-fed lake in the north of Utror, reached on foot from Ladu. It is the source of the Utror khwar. It sits at 9,950 feet. A folktale tells of a golden bowl. The lake is only accessible in summer. Access is by four-wheel drive to Ladu, then a 4 to 6 hour hike.

Laddu Lake is a small natural water body at the head of the Laddu valley, south of Utror. The Laddu Khwar stream drains the same valley. Access is on foot from Laddu village; no mapped path reaches the lake.

Laddu is a hamlet and trailhead above Utror. The jeep track ends here; the walk to Laddu Lake begins. An information board and Laddu Hut guesthouse lie a few hundred metres north-east. Access is by jeep track from Utror.

Mahodand Lake is a large glacial lake at the head of the Ushu valley. It lies about 40 kilometres from Kalam in the Usho sub-valley, at an elevation of about 2,865 metres. In summer it is popular for boating and camping. Access is by four wheel drive from Kalam, about 2 to 3 hours.

Mankial Sar is a peak. It is the second-highest in the Swat valley, east of Kalam. The highest peaks are Falak Sar and Mankial Sar. It is a mountaineering objective. The approach is via Mankial valley, expedition-style.

Matiltan is a village in the Ushu valley. It has a hydropower plant and glacier views. Falak Sar is visible from it, about 11 kilometres from Kalam. It is a stop on the jeep road to Mahodand. The village is reached by a non-metalled road in a four-wheel drive vehicle from Kalam. It is open in summer and autumn.
Mushroom Lake is a remote mushroom-shaped alpine lake in the upper Gabral and Shahi Bagh valley. The hike from Shahi Bagh takes 10 hours.
Pearl Lake is a small lake in the hills north of Kalam on the OSM map. Access is by hike in summer.
Spin Khwar Lake, also Spinkhor, is a small lake and stream near Kundol. The Spinkhor waterfall is nearby, named near Kundol Lake. Reach it by a short hike off the Kundol trail, in summer.
Thal is a village in Kumrat, the valley's last settlement and its entry point. It is home to a wooden mosque. The paved road from Dir ends here; beyond lies a jeep track.
Thalo Zom is a glaciated 6,000 metres peak at the head of the Gabral/Kumrat divide. Access is expedition terrain.

Ushu is a village at the edge of the Ushu forest, on the road to Mahodand and Saifullah lakes. The Ushu glacier snow closes it in winter. The glacier blocks the only path to Mahodand. Ushu is known for its cloudy, rainy forest. Access is by 4 wheel drive jeep from Kalam via Matiltan, in summer only.

Utror is a village and green side valley of waterfalls and pastures west of Kalam. It is the trail head for Kundol, Izmis and Katora lakes and the road to Badgoi Pass. Badogai Pass connects it to Upper Dir. Utror lies 16 kilometres from Kalam. A jeep road runs from Kalam; access is in summer and autumn.
